messages.subject: [Traminer-users] remove titles from subplots
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This cannot be done using the group argument. You will need to do the plotting separately for each category. For instance, if you want to group according to the gcse5eq covariate which has two levels:

Group <- factor(mvad$gcse5eq)

par(mfrow=c(nlevels(Group),1)) ##Layout of the plots
for(ll in levels(Group)){ ## The plots are done in the same order as levels()
seqdplot(mvadseq[Group==ll, ], with.legend=FALSE, use.layout=FALSE)
}

Hope this helsp,
Matthias

Objet : [Traminer-users] remove titles from subplots

Hi,

Does anyone know how to remove the subtitles from the subplots that are created with the group option in the seqdplot command?  I didn't see any mention of them in the par help file.  Perhaps I have to do this by somehow removing the labels from the grouping variable?  I have pasted code for an example graph below.

Thanks,

Jeremy


library(TraMineR)
library(WeightedCluster)
data(mvad)
mvad.alphabet <- c("employment", "FE", "HE", "joblessness", "school", "training")
mvad.labels <- c("Employment", "Further Education", "Higher Education", "Joblessness", "School", "Training")
mvad.scodes <- c("EM", "FE", "HE", "JL", "SC", "TR")
mvadseq <- seqdef(mvad[, 17:86], alphabet = mvad.alphabet, states = mvad.scodes, labels = mvad.labels, weights = mvad$weight, xtstep = 6)

#Defining the custom cost matrix
subm.custom <- matrix(
  c(0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1,
    1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2,
    1, 1, 0, 3, 1, 2,
    2, 2, 3, 0, 3, 1,
    1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 2,
    1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 0),
  nrow = 6, ncol = 6, byrow = TRUE)

mvaddist1.0 <- seqdist(mvadseq, method = "OM", indel = 1.0, sm = subm.custom)
pamclust1.0 <- wcKMedRange(mvaddist1.0, kvals = 2:10, weights = mvad$weight)

seqdplot(mvadseq, group = pamclust1.0$clustering$cluster4, border=NA)

messages.subject: [Traminer-users] New in TraMineRextras: Position-wise group-typical states
messages.subject_clean: [Traminer-users] New in TraMineRextras: Position-wise group-typical states
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

"Position wise group-typical states" aims at looking at and visualizing the relationship between a state sequences and a covariate. It can also be used to identify position-wise differences between clusters. The method was introduced in Studer (2015) under the name "sequence of typical state" and is now available in the latest version of TraMineRextras.

A short vignette is available here:
http://mephisto.unige.ch/pub/publications/Matthias/typicalstate.pdf

For a short try, run :
library(TraMineRextras)
data(mvad)
mvad.seq <- seqdef(mvad, 17:86, xtstep = 6)
mvad.si <- seqimplic(mvad.seq, group=mvad$gcse5eq)
plot(mvad.si, lwd=3)

All the best,
Matthias


Matthias Studer (2015), Comment: On the Use of Globally Interdependent Multiple Sequence Analysis, Sociological Methodology 45, DOI: 10.1177/0081175015588095

messages.subject: [Traminer-users]  setting unegual "space" parameter in seqIplot
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

When plotting sequences with seqIplot, I'd like to set a changing
value for the ?space? parameter. (My aim is to group graphically the
sequences by pairs.) It works but :
* there're an error message and 2 warning messages
* y-labels disappear
See example below.

Is there any other way to do so?

Thanks!
S?bastien


MWE : 

data(mvad)
s <- seqdef(mvad[1:10, 17:86])
seqIplot(s, space = .4 )                        # constant space value, everything goes right
seqIplot(s, space =  c(0, rep(c(0, .4), 4)) )   # changing space value, it works, but the y-labels aren't displayed

messages.subject: [Traminer-users] remove titles from subplots
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Just in case someone else is also interested in removing titles from subplots, I found that the par function can be used to hide the titles by making them white so they blend into the background (see below).  It would be better to remove them entirely, but changing the color seems to work ok.

Jeremy

library(TraMineR)
library(WeightedCluster)
data(mvad)
mvad.alphabet <- c("employment", "FE", "HE", "joblessness", "school", "training")
mvad.labels <- c("Employment", "Further Education", "Higher Education", "Joblessness", "School", "Training")
mvad.scodes <- c("EM", "FE", "HE", "JL", "SC", "TR")
mvadseq <- seqdef(mvad[, 17:86], alphabet = mvad.alphabet, states = mvad.scodes, labels = mvad.labels, weights = mvad$weight, xtstep = 6)

#Defining the custom cost matrix
subm.custom <- matrix(
  c(0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1,
    1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2,
    1, 1, 0, 3, 1, 2,
    2, 2, 3, 0, 3, 1,
    1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 2,
    1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 0),
  nrow = 6, ncol = 6, byrow = TRUE)

mvaddist1.0 <- seqdist(mvadseq, method = "OM", indel = 1.0, sm = subm.custom)
pamclust1.0 <- wcKMedRange(mvaddist1.0, kvals = 2:10, weights = mvad$weight)

par(col.main="white")
seqdplot(mvadseq, group = pamclust1.0$clustering$cluster4, border=NA)
